question.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the $3$rd term is $36$ and the common ratio is $3?$
question.worked_solution:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine ${a}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\ 36 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {3}^{(3-1)} \\ 36 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {3}^{2} \\ 36 & =9{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =4\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=4$ and $r=3.$ Substituting our values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{4(1-{3}^{N})}{1-3} \\  & =\frac{4}{(-2)}(1-{3}^{N}) \\  & =-2(1-{3}^{N}) \\  & =2({3}^{N}-1)\end{aligned}
$$
